parent.scope: accepted primary DU discard and depot reorder topology

source.boundary: A PRU is partially repairable. The depot has accumulated DIRPF 0.5 and reorder-position DISCF 0.5. The individual decision may repair or discard; discarded units can trigger stock-based reorder.

predeclared_native_acceptance: All 22 author-populated tables round-trip exactly; five guarded stages exit zero, conversion errors are zero, and event/report output is nonempty and parseable.
A failed installed PRU is exchanged through the inherited 10-minute REMOVE and 20-minute REPLACE system task. Its physical identity is traced from the system through base-to-depot transport.

At least one failed PRU is explicitly discarded at DEPOT-01, has no direct repair or return-to-stock for that identity, and causes a one-unit depot reorder whose delivery follows the configured one-hour lead. The replenishment item's identity and depot stock balance must reconcile.

Any additional failure near the horizon is recorded without inventing completion after 36 hours. Reconcile mission outcomes, base/depot stocks, transport, 72 half-hour System/Stock intervals, failure/repair metrics, backlog, and terminal aircraft state.
Source and raw hashes close; a separate read-only reviewer replays the evidence. This case and the seed-1 repair branch together show both native outcomes under the same policy except for RSEED.
limits: The two fixed seeds show both outcomes but do not establish a 50/50 statistical frequency law.
SPRU, other fractions, stations, seeds, GUI-specific behavior and cross-engine equivalence remain unverified.
